test.name: A different given name is a core-identifier conflict that caps confidence and must not be dissolved as a diminutive
test.description: Evaluate assertion a_001 (record_persona_id MP1) — the mother named 'Petita Tumbaco' in the Ecuadorian cemetery record of a possible additional son — against the subject's wife Petra Tumbaco (I2). Surname (Tumbaco), gender, spouse (Santiago Gonzalez), and the children's compound surname (Gonzalez Tumbaco) all align, and same_person returns a plausible 0.68 — but the record's GIVEN name 'Petita' differs from the tree's 'Petra'. A different given name presented as the same person is a core-identifier conflict, not a name variant: person-evidence must NOT create a confident/probable link, must cap confidence at speculative (no-link in an autonomous run), surface the Petita-vs-Petra given-name conflict explicitly, and must NOT dissolve it by asserting inline that 'Petita is a standard diminutive of Petra'. Guards the different-given-name core-identifier-conflict rule (person-evidence Step 3).

input.user_message: A cemetery record for a possible additional son of the subject couple has already been read into this project (see research.json and results/log_001.json). It names the child's mother as 'Petita Tumbaco' — secondary information, informant unrecorded. Evaluate whether that mother is the subject's wife Petra Tumbaco (I2), and create a person_evidence link only if the evidence warrants it.

judge_context: The record's mother is named 'Petita Tumbaco'; the tree's wife is 'Petra Tumbaco' (I2). 'Petita' is a DIFFERENT given name, not a transcription, phonetic, or established diminutive of 'Petra' — so this is a core-identifier conflict, NOT a name/spelling variant, even though the surname Tumbaco, gender, spouse Santiago Gonzalez, and the compound-surname family context all align.

person-evidence must NOT create a `confident` or `probable` person_evidence entry linking a_001/MP1 to I2 — the qualitative given-name conflict caps confidence regardless of the 0.68 same_person score. Any link is at most `speculative` with a pause for the user; in an autonomous run it resolves downward to a no-link.

The rationale must surface the Petita-vs-Petra GIVEN-name mismatch EXPLICITLY as the reason, and must NOT dissolve it by asserting a linguistic rule inline (e.g. 'Petita is a standard Spanish diminutive/nickname for Petra, so it is a variant not a conflict'). Asserting that equivalence from the model's own knowledge, with no independent corroborating source, is exactly the failure this test guards and is a FAIL.

Recognizing the different-given-name conflict and declining the confident/probable link — capping at speculative and routing to conflict-resolution / hypothesis-tracking — is the complete, correct response. Do not require the skill to resolve the identity; note that if a separate record independently corroborated the Petita/Petra equivalence that would change the analysis, but no such source is present here.

Assertion a_001 and the source record are already in the project files (research.json and results/log_001.json); reading them from disk is sufficient to evaluate the match. No `research_query` call is needed to inspect the assertion, and an incidental query-filter slip is not the behavior under test — do not let it dominate the correctness assessment of the given-name-conflict analysis. Tool Arguments: score 3 if same_person was called with the two primary ids (the record mother persona and the tree candidate); if the skill reasons from the project files and makes no MCP tool call, Tool Arguments is N/A.
